newsitem.title: USA: Dole says he will debate trade with Clinton.
newsitem.headline: Dole says he will debate trade with Clinton.

text.p: Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole, talking economics in the vote-rich U.S. heartland on Friday, said he would press his case for a more aggressive trade policy in upcoming presidential debates.

"We've got to be more aggressive in our trade policies and that will probably be a subject of some debates when we have debates between myself and President Bill Clinton," Dole told a voter forum arranged by his campaign at Hill Manufacturing, a plant in Wauseon, near Toledo in northwestern Ohio.

"We've seen the trade deficit grow and grow and grow in the Clinton administration," Dole said. He told the audience a tougher trade policy would go hand-in-hand with his tax-cutting economic programme to create jobs.

"You have what now, 50 employees, probably after my plan, a couple of years, I'll just take a guess here, you may be up to 60, 65. You're going to make a little more profit. You can expand the business. We're going to have an aggressive trade policy too, that may be helpful," he said.
"When you add it all up, we think it's going to create the growth that we need in America."

Dole also renewed his call for a bipartisan commission to reform Medicare and charged that Clinton campaign ads deceived senior citizens into believing the Republicans would gut the old-age health programme. "Take it (Medicare) out of politics. Stop scaring senior citizens," he said.
Dole began the day in Montpelier, Ohio, where he met some distant relatives for breakfast at a Main Street restaurant. He had paid a visit to an ancestral home and gravesite the night before.

After chatting through breakfast without eating, Dole stopped off at a donut shop and bought three large trays of baked treats for himself and his entourage. Later in the day, he was to campaign in Michigan and Illinois.

With his roots in the Midwest, Dole shows a clear affinity for voters in small towns and rural areas. A country song that frequently accompanies his appearances in the region contains the lines, "Sing a song about the heartland ... the only place I feel at home."
At a county fair in Montpelier on Thursday evening, he roamed eagerly, shaking hands with enthusiastic crowds long after speaking at a rally.

Dole trails Clinton in recent polls in all three states where he campaigned on Friday. In Ohio, which has 21 electoral votes out 270 needed for election, Clinton led by 42 percentage points to 36 in an early August Mason-Dixon poll.

In Michigan, with 18 electoral votes, Clinton led 47 to 29 in an EPIC/MRA Mason-Dixon poll last week, and in Illinois, with 22 electoral votes, Clinton had a 54-33 lead in a Mason-Dixon poll last week.
